title: Modernising the Architecture: RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU and the KV Cache
summary: Upgrade the tiny GPT into a Llama-style model one component at a time: RMSNorm for LayerNorm, rotary embeddings for the learned position table, a SwiGLU feed-forward network, then a KV cache, a sliding window with attention sinks and a rolling buffer for fast, bounded-memory generation. Each change is derived, worked by hand and implemented in PyTorch.
objectives: Implement RMSNorm and RoPE in PyTorch and verify that rotated query-key scores depend only on relative position
Implement a SwiGLU feed-forward network and size its hidden layer at about 8d/3 to match a 4d GELU FFN's parameters
Add a KV cache to attention, split generation into prefill and decode, and prove it correct by comparing greedy outputs with and without the cache
Build a sliding-window mask with attention sinks and explain why evicting the first tokens breaks a streaming model
Implement a circular rolling-buffer cache and explain why slot order does not affect attention
prerequisites: You should have built the baseline model in [Attention in Code](/learn/model-foundations/attention-in-code) and [Train a Tiny GPT](/learn/model-foundations/train-a-tiny-gpt). The theory behind each upgrade is in [The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block) (LayerNorm and RMSNorm, the feed-forward network, position information) and [Context Windows, Prefill and the KV Cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache). This lesson follows `llm_from_scratch/part_3/`.
